method.arm_prose: In a throwaway detached worktree every docstring became '' and every non-pragma comment was removed in 800 of 820 tracked non-test, non-src/rnd .py files (the other 20 had neither); line numbers preserved, stripped AST equal modulo docstrings (checked per file, 0 skipped). Unit+cosa tier run sharded in both arms; a test is prose-dependent iff red when stripped and green in a per-file run of the unstripped tree.
method.arm_phase4: Same 1,588 files with the 45 Phase 4 pages blanked to one line (src/docs/*.md minus fastapi/api.*, both CLAUDE.md, README.md, src/cosa/README.md, src/workflow/agentic-voice-workflow.md), compared with unstripped per-file runs.

caveats: The strip simulates a docs-only rewrite; it cannot see tests that only pass because wording survives a paraphrase.
Several shards were SIGKILLed by a cgroup cap (rc=137); every killed shard's files were re-run per-file to completion, in both arms.

Source-text readers that assert code (not prose) are unaffected by a docs-only rewrite and are not listed as dependents; scan.py found 443 candidate functions in 428 files that read source and assert a phrase, scan2.py found 52 with a literal that lives only in a docstring/comment of a resolved target, and the mutation arm confirmed which of those actually break (the others assert code text that also appears in executable tokens, or assert absence).
method.population_326: scan.py and scan2.py ran over ALL 1,914 test files by git ls-files. On the 326 files outside src/tests/unit and src/cosa/tests (e2e_ui 116, smoke 97, integration 59, cosa 10, parity_oracle 9, websocket_smoke 7, parity_oracle_fullpage 6, lupin_smoke 4, manual 4, e2e 3, ws_channel_browser 3, and 8 singletons) the scan returned 64 files that read something and assert a substring, 0 with a literal that lives only in a docstring/comment of a resolved target, and 0 with a __doc__/getdoc/get_docstring call. They were NOT executed under either mutation arm: the population is CHECKED STATICALLY, UNVERIFIED BY MUTATION.
